question: What makes an abortion officially classified as 'unsafe' by global health standards?

options.A: Any pregnancy loss occurring naturally during the first trimester
options.B: A procedure done by unskilled persons or in poor environments
options.C: A termination done without proper surgical instruments
options.D: A medical termination performed past the first trimester

explanation: An unsafe abortion happens when the procedure is carried out by people without proper training, in dirty or poorly equipped places, or both. Knowing this helps us understand why access to safe care is so vital! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h1)

question: Why do many young women and teenagers in Nigeria end up turning to unsafe abortion methods?

options.A: Preference for traditional herbal remedies over modern medicine
options.B: Easy availability of safe surgical clinics in rural areas
options.C: Lack of financial resources and reproductive health access
options.D: Strict enforcement of mandatory hospital reporting laws

explanation: Poverty, fear of social stigma, and struggling to find safe, legal services often push vulnerable girls into dangerous alternatives. As nurses, keeping our clinics open and welcoming is key to changing this. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h1)

question: In most parts of Nigeria, under what single major condition is an abortion legally permitted?

options.A: When both parents agree in writing before the first trimester
options.B: When the woman is below the age of consent
options.C: When the pregnancy results from an act of sexual assault
options.D: When the procedure is strictly necessary to save the woman's life

explanation: Nigerian law is quite strict, usually only allowing an abortion if the continuation of the pregnancy directly threatens the mother's life. It's an important legal boundary every nurse practicing here should know. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h2)

question: How does the strict criminalization of abortion in Nigeria directly affect patient health outcomes?

options.A: It encourages traditional healers to adopt modern sterile surgical techniques
options.B: It guarantees that all post-abortion patients receive free government care
options.C: It forces patients to seek secretive care, leading to dangerous treatment delays
options.D: It completely eliminates the practice of illegal pregnancy terminations

explanation: Because of fear of arrest, women often hide what they've done and only come to the hospital when complications become life-threatening. Compassionate, confidential nursing care can help break down this fear! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h2)

question: Which immediate complication happens when an instrument accidentally punctures the muscular wall of the uterus during a procedure?
explanation: Uterine perforation occurs when sharp instruments or foreign objects poke a hole right through the wall of the uterus. It's a surgical emergency you'll want to watch out for during recovery! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h3)

question: A patient arrives at the emergency ward with a high fever, foul-smelling vaginal discharge, and tummy pain after a clandestine abortion. What is your top nursing priority?

options.A: Immediate scheduling for cosmetic scar revision
options.B: Documenting the identity of the illegal practitioner

explanation: Fever and foul discharge are classic red flags for a severe infection or sepsis. Stabilizing the patient and starting broad-spectrum antibiotics comes before anything else! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h3)

question: What is a very common long-term problem for women who survive an untreated pelvic infection after an unsafe abortion?
explanation: Severe pelvic infections can leave behind scar tissue that blocks the fallopian tubes, making it very difficult for the woman to get pregnant in the future. Early infection treatment is a lifesaver for fertility! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h4)

question: A patient who previously had a secretive abortion now struggles with recurrent miscarriages in her second trimester. What underlying issue should you suspect?

options.A: Primary ovarian failure due to hormonal imbalances
options.B: Chronic renal failure from past chemical toxicity
options.C: Acquired uterine fibroids from retained tissue
options.D: Cervical incompetence from past traumatic dilation

explanation: If the cervix was forced open too aggressively during a past procedure, the tissues can become weak, causing it to open prematurely in later pregnancies. You'll learn to spot this history during antenatal booking! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h4)

question: What factor makes the emotional and mental distress much worse for patients recovering from an unsafe abortion in Nigeria?

options.A: Social stigma and fear of legal consequences
options.C: Mandatory psychological screening in government hospitals
options.D: Immediate support from community religious leaders

explanation: Fear of being arrested, judged, or rejected by loved ones forces many women to hide their pain and suffer all alone. As nurses, being a safe, listening ear makes all the difference. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h5)

question: Why is it so important for nurses to check in on a patient's mental health during post-abortion care?

options.A: Patients with mental distress are legally barred from receiving contraceptives
options.B: Psychological symptoms interfere directly with the absorption of oral antibiotics
options.C: Hospital insurance policies refuse to pay claims without a mental health diagnosis
options.D: Physical healing alone does not address hidden trauma, anxiety, and depression

explanation: Treating the physical body is only half the job. The secrecy and stress surrounding unsafe abortions leave deep emotional wounds that also need healing and gentle support. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h5)

question: When a patient is suspected of having an unsafe abortion, what should be the primary goal of your first nursing assessment?

options.A: Identifying life-threatening complications and vital sign instability
options.B: Reporting the patient's family members to hospital authorities
options.C: Collecting evidence for police investigation and legal prosecution
options.D: Determining the exact herbal concoction ingested by the patient

explanation: In an emergency, airway, breathing, circulation, and watching for heavy bleeding or sepsis always come first. A nurse's duty is to save the patient's life, not play detective! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h6)

question: Why must you always maintain a non-judgmental and confidential attitude when taking a patient's history?

options.A: To prevent the patient from requesting discharge against medical advice
options.B: To comply with international nursing board regulations on patient billing
options.C: To encourage honest disclosure of the abortion method and ensure prompt treatment
options.D: To help the hospital avoid paying malpractice insurance premiums

explanation: If patients think you will judge or report them, they will lie or hide what happened—and that can cost them their lives. Trust and confidentiality save lives in the ward! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h6)

question: What are the three core components of the standard Post-Abortion Care (PAC) model?

options.A: Surgical sterilization, mandatory psychiatric evaluation, and legal reporting
options.B: Emergency treatment, family planning counseling, and reproductive health linkage
options.C: Antenatal booking, nutritional rehabilitation, and infant immunization
options.D: Blood transfusion, long-term hospitalization, and vocational training

explanation: PAC is a complete package: treat the immediate emergency, talk about family planning so it doesn't happen again, and connect the patient to ongoing health care. You'll see this model everywhere in public health! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h7)

question: A patient with an incomplete abortion has stable vital signs and no signs of severe infection. Which procedure is best for clearing her uterus?
explanation: Manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) is a quick, safe, and gentle method to clear out the remaining tissue in uncomplicated cases without needing heavy surgery. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h7)

question: What is the most effective way for nurses to help prevent unsafe abortions in the community?

options.A: Providing accessible family planning education and modern contraception
options.B: Reporting all suspected cases of premarital sex to local community elders
options.C: Enforcing strict hospital visitation limits for young unmarried females
options.D: Promoting traditional herbal remedies as safe alternatives for fertility control

explanation: The best cure is prevention! When young people have easy access to modern family planning and accurate education, the rate of unintended pregnancies—and unsafe abortions—drops dramatically. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of setting up youth-friendly reproductive health clinics in local communities?

options.A: To offer young people a safe, non-judgmental space to access contraception and information
options.B: To track and penalize adolescents who engage in early sexual activity
options.C: To distribute free surgical instruments for home use
options.D: To provide mandatory pregnancy testing for all high school graduates

explanation: Youth-friendly clinics take away the fear of judgment and stigma, making it easy for teenagers to ask questions and get reliable health guidance early on. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h8)
